picks.rationale: Both sides now move for summary judgment in the Authors Guild/OpenAI case — the ruling that will set the fair-use line every author and publisher plans around.
picks.excerpt: The Authors Guild and 13 co-plaintiffs including Jonathan Franzen and George R.R. Martin, along with OpenAI and Microsoft, have all asked a U.S. District Court for summary judgment on data scraping, copyright, and fair use.
picks.title: Authors Guild, Co-Plaintiffs Seek Summary Judgment in OpenAI Case

picks.rationale: Axel Scheffler puts a named, working illustrator's economics on the record — the clearest creator-side case yet for why picture-book commissioning has to change now.
picks.excerpt: Illustrator Axel Scheffler argues generative AI is a real and immediate threat to the livelihoods of book illustrators, and calls on government to act.
picks.title: AI is a real threat to illustrators, and the government must act

picks.rationale: A named framework from one of the largest publishers tells authors and editors exactly which AI uses are allowed and which must be disclosed — a rulebook you can act on tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: Springer Nature has published a framework setting out how AI should be used across its publishing operations and by its authors.
picks.title: Springer Nature launches framework on use of artificial intelligence
picks._note: The Bookseller's OUP guideline update (2026-09-12, already published) is a different publisher and a different document; kept as distinct.

picks.rationale: Rare hard number on AI in publishing operations — 50,000 books a month through one platform — and a vendor pitching human support as the differentiator.
picks.excerpt: Veristage says publishers now process the equivalent of more than 50,000 books per month through Insight, its AI publishing services platform — a U.S.-based AI-driven publishing services company that answers the phone.
picks.title: An AI Company That Picks Up the Phone: PW Talks with Hannah Johnson

picks.rationale: Sanctions land on a professional who shipped LLM-invented sources — the sharpest reminder that anyone drafting with AI owns every citation in the manuscript.
picks.excerpt: A lawyer was sanctioned after ChatGPT-generated filings cited fake testimony from witnesses who never existed — a cautionary tale for anyone drafting with an LLM.
picks.title: ChatGPT-using lawyer punished for citing fake testimony from made-up witnesses
